summary: Astrid Zotter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Leipzig. She held positions at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).
Athanaric Huard is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Georges-Jean Pinault. He served as an Assistent at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Atsuhiko Yoshida (b. 1934), a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology, studied at Seikei and Tokyo Universities, Strasbourg, and under Georges Dumézil at the CNRS (~1960–1967). He later served as professor at Seikei (1970) and Gakushuin (2006).

Atsuki Nakagami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakagami held posts as a visiting researcher at the University of Hamburg (attested 2022) and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Atsushi Ibuki (b. 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and became a professor at Toyo University around 2005.

Atsushi Kanazawa (b. 1951), an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1980). Kanazawa taught at the Meteorological College (~1988–1993) and served as lecturer, assistant professor, and professor at Komazawa University from ~1987 onward.

Atsushi Kiyozawa (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Delhi and served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).

Atsushi Uno (b. 1922), an Indologist and philosopher, studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu Universities under T. R. V. Murti, Raghunath Giri, and others. He held professorships at Tokai (1971), Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai (~1986–1993).

Atsuuji Ashikaga (1901–1983) was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Ryosaburo Sakaki, completed degrees at Doshisha and Kyoto Universities, and held multiple professorial and administrative posts at Kyoto University from 1930.
Atsuyoshi Keika (b. 1944) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who served at Otani University as a lecturer (attested 1990) and professor (attested 2014).

Atul Chandra Chatterjee (1874–1955) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Charles Henry Tawney at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, then attended King's College, Cambridge, before serving in the Indian Civil Service (~1897–1931).

August Boeckh (1785–1867), a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher at Halle-Wittenberg. He held faculty posts at Heidelberg University (1807–1811) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811–1861).

August Conrady (1864–1925) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Würzburg and Leipzig, he held posts at Peking University (1903–1904) and the University of Leipzig, where he became a professor in 1920.

August Dillmann (1823–1894), a scholar of linguistics and religious studies, studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, Kiel, and Giessen, before serving at Frederick William University Berlin (~1869–1894).

August Ferdinand Naeke (1788–1838) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1805–1810) and held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1817–1818) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1838).

August Fick (1833–1916) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (1852–1856). He later held professorships at the University of Göttingen (from 1876) and the University of Breslau (1888–1891).
August Fischer (1865–1949) was a scholar of linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1886–1889) and held a post at the University of Leipzig (~1900–1930).

August Friedrich Pott (1802–1887) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Göttingen and under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He lectured in Berlin (1830) before serving as a professor at Halle-Wittenberg from 1833.

August Hermann Francke (1870–1930) was a Tibetologist, linguist, and historian. Educated at Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and Humboldt University of Berlin, he later served as a Privatdozent (1922) and extraordinary professor (1925) at Humboldt University of Berlin.

August Hjalmar Edgren (1840–1903) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, and under William Dwight Whitney at Yale. He taught at Yale, Lund, and Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as Rector of the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).
